reviewType: INDEPENDENT-ADVERSARIAL — reviewer did not author the subject; posture was to reject
verdictStatement: The blocker v10 was authored to close is CLOSED, and I could not falsify it. My own sweep over all 116 evidence-leaf positions — whole program, fresh subprocess per candidate — rejected 116 of 116 by a finding NAMING the position, against 87 admitted under the predecessor. Every central claim in the dispatch is true and several are precise to the leaf: the 116 = 102 + 10 nulls + 4 empty containers partition reproduces exactly; the three worst leaves are double-gated and name the independently measured value; fileResolves/anchorResolves/registerBinding are genuinely recomputed from disk and the live register, which I proved by perturbing disk state rather than the declaration; all three boolean/integer arms are 0 admitted on v10 while reproducing the predecessor's 15/139 exactly; the carry claims are byte-exact; V4 is genuinely unaffected. The single blocker is that v10's OWN new evidence block reproduces B-VER9R-01 in miniature. Of its 316 leaf positions, 79 sit in four registry loops sized from the artifact rather than from a measurement, so VER10-COVER cannot fire in them by construction, and the block's measured partition is computed, printed in the PASS banner, and compared against nothing. I planted a claim that this successor 'has been independently re-reviewed and PASSED', fabricated a residual restatement asserting a residual is closed, and silently deleted a freeze §7.2 recorded input — each exits 0 with the full green banner. As in the v9 review, the contract needs almost no byte change to clear this; the checker does.
reHashDiscipline: freeze §7.2.1. Both subjects were hashed at review start, snapshotted to a scratchpad copy of the whole tree, and re-hashed at review end. Both were byte-identical at both readings and match the dispatch digests exactly. claim-register.v1.json did NOT drift during my window (20ab0c31…, unchanged from the end of the v9 review). No subject moved, so no re-baselining was required.

blockers.theClaimUnderTest: check-versioning-v10.py docstring: 'The same discipline is applied to v10's own new evidence block.' successorRevision.evidenceEnforcementRepair.checkerDisposition.checkerEnforcesEveryDeclaredEvidenceLeaf = true. R-VER10-02: 'The partition scope is the 3 sub-blocks named in evidenceLeafEnforcement.scope plus the whole of successorRevision.evidenceEnforcementRepair.'
blockers.whatTheDisciplineActuallyIs: Two mechanisms make the 116-position result trustworthy, and I verified BOTH work inside the declared evidence scope. (1) VER10-COVER: a leaf position with no registry entry is itself a finding, so the partition cannot silently shrink or grow. (2) VER10-PART: the declared partition is compared against the computed one. Neither is operative for the v10 block.
mechanismOfTheDefect: evidence_registry() is built from measurements — audit rows derived from disk, exit-class lists derived from the D9 span — so the registry has a FIXED shape and any position the artifact adds has no entry and fires VER10-COVER. I confirmed this: adding directionPreservation.adversarialExtra fires VER10-COVER (plus VER10-CARRY).

enforcement_registry() builds four of its loops from the ARTIFACT'S OWN list lengths: `residualRestatements[index]` (line ~839), `recordedInputs[index]` (line ~847), `retainedResiduals[index]` (line ~858) and `notClaimed[index]` (line ~875) all iterate `range(len(<artifact list>))`. The registry therefore GROWS WITH the artifact, so VER10-COVER is structurally unreachable for every position inside them.

evaluate() returns `new_partition` for the ENFORCE scope and check() stores it in LAST['newPartition']. main() prints it in the PASS banner ('v10 enforcement record: 316 leaf positions — 228 MEASURED, 60 GROUNDED, 28 UNMEASURABLE') and NOTHING compares it to anything. The VER10-PART loop at lines ~1384-1393 reads only `partition` (the 116 scope). The number 316 does not occur anywhere in versioning-policy.v10.json.

successorRevision.evidenceEnforcementRepair.recordedInputs has no required-name set, unlike successorRevision.d9CitationRepair.recordedInputs, which is checked at lines ~1295-1312 against nine pinned names plus the register. So a §7.2 recording obligation can be dropped from the v10 record and nothing notices.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: 4. R-VER10-08 — the hard-vs-semantic gate split. THE RULING.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE SPLIT IS PRINCIPLED AND I UPHOLD IT — but for a sharper reason than the author gives, and it is brittle in a way the disclosure understates.
whatIReproduced: Repointing the register's ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS binding to artifacts/retention-tiers.v23.json reproduces the author's demonstration EXACTLY: 'VER10-LEAF: successorRevision.d9CitationRepair.siblingCitationAudit.entries[6].registerBinding declares "artifacts/retention-tiers.v22.json"; this checker measured "artifacts/retention-tiers.v23.json" from disk', exit 1. Single finding, correctly named.

The coupling is LIVE, not hypothetical, and the trigger is armed: retention-tiers.v23.json (3f8c1df5…) AND check-retention-custody-v23.py are BOTH already on disk while claim-register.v1.json still binds ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS to retention-tiers.v22.json.
The author's benign-drift claim is CONFIRMED: I added a 34th claim leaving D9/VERSIONING/ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS alone and check-versioning-v10.py stays at exit 0 with the full green banner.

TWO FURTHER TRIGGERS the residual does not enumerate. (a) I added an EVALUATION-PROOF -> evaluation-proof.v13.json claim to the register — an ADDITION, not a repoint — and got 'VER10-LEAF: … entries[5].registerBinding declares null; this checker measured "artifacts/evaluation-proof.v13.json" from disk', exit 1. (b) measure_audit() resolves bare labels by artifact family with `hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None`, so a SECOND retention-tiers-family binding would collapse entry[6] to null and also exit 1. R-VER10-08 says 'if the coordinator repoints either', which covers neither case.
centralClaimAdjudications.theBrittlenessTheDisclosureUnderstates: v10 is not merely 'red until a successor is authored'. It is UNREPAIRABLE IN PLACE. I applied the obvious one-line fix — update the declared entries[6].registerBinding to v23 to match the measurement — and got a TEN-finding cascade, not silence: VER10-CARRY (the leaf is not in ENUMERATED_DELTA and must be byte-identical to v9), then VER10-LEAF and VER10-PROSE on enumeratedDelta[8], [9] and [10] as the sorted delta list shifts by one index, then VER10-LEAF on enumeratedDeltaCount (11 vs 12), then two VER10-COVER findings for the now-expected enumeratedDelta[11]. The cause is that ENUMERATED_DELTA is a CONSTANT INSIDE THE CHECKER and the artifact's enumeratedDelta table is index-position-compared against sorted(moved). So the repair requires a coordinated edit of BOTH files — a new checker AND a new artifact version AND a fresh independent review. R-VER10-08 says 'the repair is a successor that re-measures the audit', which is literally correct, but a reader would reasonably infer a one-line artifact edit, and would be wrong.

theRuling.principle: The axis that actually separates these two cases is WHAT THE DECLARATION IS A STATEMENT ABOUT, and on that axis v10 lands correctly in both.
theRuling.measurementsGetHardComparison: siblingCitationAudit.entries[*].registerBinding is a RECORDED MEASUREMENT — 'at authoring, the register bound X'. A recorded measurement that is never compared against the thing it measured is not evidence, it is prose that looks like evidence. That is precisely B-VER9R-01. When the register moves, the record now says something FALSE about the world, so exit 1 is a TRUE POSITIVE about these bytes, not a false alarm about the register. Hard comparison is right.
theRuling.invariantsGetSemanticGates: decisionDependencies[4].source against the register's live D9 binding is a CONTINUING INVARIANT — 'this citation is the register-bound head'. It must hold across time, so it is correctly gated on the semantic property rather than on a register digest. R-VER9-07 was vindicated three times: a byte pin would have failed on the very repoint it anticipates. Semantic gating is right.
theRuling.verdictOnTheSplit: PRINCIPLED, not ad hoc. The author's stated justification — 'leaving it uncompared IS B-VER9R-01' — is correct but incomplete: it explains why the register binding is hard-compared without explaining why D9 is not, which invites the reading that the choice was convenience. The measurement/invariant distinction is the real principle and it should be stated, because it is what makes the split defensible rather than lucky.
theRuling.isItBrittleAgainstAScheduledEvent: Yes, and deliberately so, and I do NOT ask for it to be weakened. Weakening the register comparison to keep the checker green across coordinator acts is exactly the defect under repair. What I do ask is that the brittleness be recorded at its true blast radius — unrepairable in place, requiring a coordinated checker+artifact successor — rather than as one finding at one entry.
theRuling.recommendedRepairNotRequired: Record the measurement with its own as-of provenance: carry registerBinding alongside the register digest it was measured against, so a stale reading reports as 'measured against register 20ab0c31…, which has since moved' rather than as an undifferentiated leaf mismatch. That preserves the true positive, tells the successor author exactly what to re-measure, and decouples the repair from the enumeratedDelta index cascade. This is a design improvement, non-blocking.

nonBlockingObservations.title: R-VER10-08's blast radius is understated: the in-place repair is a 10-finding cascade, and the true repair requires editing the CHECKER.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Updating entries[6].registerBinding to v23 after a repoint produces VER10-CARRY plus VER10-LEAF/VER10-PROSE on enumeratedDelta[8], [9] and [10], plus VER10-LEAF on enumeratedDeltaCount (11 vs 12), plus two VER10-COVER findings for enumeratedDelta[11] — because ENUMERATED_DELTA is a checker constant and the artifact's table is index-position-compared against sorted(moved).
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: The residual's 'the repair is a successor that re-measures the audit' is literally correct, so this is not a false statement. But a reader would infer a one-line artifact edit. Recording the cascade, and that the checker must change too, would make the successor's cost visible before it is incurred.

nonBlockingObservations.title: R-VER10-08 enumerates repoints but not additions; two further register events trip it.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Adding an EVALUATION-PROOF -> evaluation-proof.v13.json claim (an addition, not a repoint) flips entries[5].registerBinding from null and exits 1 — I reproduced this. Separately, measure_audit resolves bare labels by family with `hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None`, so a second retention-tiers-family binding collapses entry[6] to null and also exits 1.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: The residual's MECHANISM description ('2 by artifact family for the bare label strings that carry no id') is accurate and does cover these structurally. Only its enumeration of trigger conditions — 'if the coordinator repoints either' — is incomplete. Given evaluation-proof.v13.json is on disk and unregistered, the EP trigger is as live as the RT one.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The --selftest banner's '9 boolean respellings' is label-string-derived and overcounts by 2.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: selftest() computes the counts with `'float' in label` and `'bool' in label or 'BOOLEAN' in label` over the mutation LABELS. Of the 9 matched: 'respell the swept boolean count as a float' is a FLOAT respelling double-counted into the boolean bucket, and 'misreport the predecessor's admitted boolean respellings' is an integer value falsification (15 -> 0), not a respelling at all. Genuine boolean respellings = 7. The 6 float count is accurate.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: Cosmetic and in the harmless direction — the boolean class IS genuinely exercised, and the separately re-derived 25-leaf sweep is the real closure evidence. But the v9 review confirmed '36 mutations, exactly 5 float' by source enumeration, and this banner would not survive the same treatment. Deriving the counts from a tag on each mutation rather than from prose would fix it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The instrument's own 'names the position' test is substring-based and can self-satisfy.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: boolean_sweep uses `tail in e` where tail is the last path segment, and MUTATIONS uses `names in e`. A leaf named `identical` is 'named' by any message containing 'byte-identical'; `version`, `total` and `source` are similarly common tokens.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: No false green resulted — I re-measured the 116 sweep and all three scalar arms with a stricter full-path criterion and got the same answers, so the reported results are sound. But the assertion is weaker than the docstring's 'names the position under test' implies, and it is the mechanism by which a future collateral rejection could be miscounted as by-position.

nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: NOT a defect and NOT an overclaim. The '0/144' claim is at exit 0 and is true. closedScalarAdmission.booleanDirection.scope and R-VER10-02 both disclose this exactly, including the 119/5 split the prior reviewer measured. nonBlockingObservations.title: The three GROUNDED-admitting carried leaves are exactly the three enumerated-delta strings — the two gates are complementary by construction.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Of 64 string leaves in the carried evidence blocks, exactly 3 admit a prose-preserving edit, and they are precisely the 3 of the 11 enumerated-delta paths whose values are strings. Every other carried prose leaf is closed by the byte-carry diff against v9.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: NOT a defect. This is a genuinely elegant property — the byte-carry diff and the GROUNDED comparator cover disjoint remainders — and R-VER10-01 states it precisely rather than rounding it off. Recorded as confirmation that the residual's reasoning, not merely its number, is correct.
